question: Building on the exercise "An application-layer flood": your Nextcloud VM's search endpoint, whose wall you have measured with ab, starts receiving a steady stream of plausible-looking queries and response times climb towards the wall. Describe the layered response you would take on the customer's side of the split: name two concrete server-side controls from this chapter (one of them the Nginx directive), explain what each does against this specific attack type, and state which evidence — from the load-measurement tools — you would use to verify that the controls worked.
sample_answer: Application-layer flood, so the customer's own configuration carries the weight. Controls: (1) rate limiting via the Nginx limit_req directive, capping requests per client where the cost arises; (2) caching, which serves repeated content cheaply and raises the effective capacity of the expensive path (timeouts/connection limits also acceptable). Verification: re-run ab and compare failed-request count, requests per second and time per request before/after; watch CPU and memory in htop/btop stay below the wall; check /var/log/nginx/access.log for capped requests. Grading: two correct customer-side controls incl. limit_req + per-control explanation tied to the attack type + at least two pieces of verification evidence.
